name: Dualizer
long_description:
Dualizer builds AI-powered, physics-based process simulation and digital twins to design and scale chemical processes and optimize existing plants. We help engineering teams identify bottlenecks, increase yield and throughput, and reduce energy and production costs—improving plant efficiency and profitability.

The platform combines AI reasoning, our proprietary deterministic simulation and optimization engine, and physics-informed machine learning. Engineers can build, calibrate, and refine models through conversation, starting from a diagram, available data, or an engineering objective. Calculations account for thermodynamics, material and energy balances, equipment behavior, and operating constraints, enabling teams to optimize interconnected equipment and operating conditions across a plant.

Equipment sizing and costing, 3D layout planning, and techno-economic analysis connect process improvements to plant-level decisions. Teams can accelerate new process scale-up, debottleneck operating plants, and continually refine operating strategies as production targets and plant conditions change. Dualizer makes rigorous simulation and optimization an ongoing capability for improving industrial productivity and profitability throughout a plant’s life.
one_liner: AI-powered physical simulation to design/optimize chemical processes

question_answers.question: How did your company get started? (i.e., How did the founders meet? How did you come up with the idea? How did you decide to be a founder?)
question_answers.answer:
All three co-founders are same school (UC Berkeley), same class (’27), same major (Chemical Engineering). Nathan and David have been classmates and friends since their first year of college and later met Chris.

The idea was simple: designing and improving chemical processes remains far too expensive, difficult, and time-consuming. We were all on paths toward PhDs, but chose to tackle this persistent industry problem as founders. We started Dualizer to bring our education and research and industry experience in process modeling, physics-based simulation, machine learning, and AI for science directly into engineering practice.

question_answers.question: What is the core problem you are solving? Why is this a big problem? What made you decide to work on it?
question_answers.answer:
Manufacturing spans an estimated **7.5 million factories worldwide across all sectors**. Process engineering underpins the production of fuels, medicines, food, cosmetics, household products, fertilizers, plastics, textiles, packaging, and advanced materials—shaping the cost and availability of everyday goods.

A large plant can require **billions of dollars to build and operate for decades**. Poor design and inefficient operation trap capital in underperforming facilities, constrain production, waste resources, and turn promising technologies into failed investments. The consequences extend across supply chains: higher prices, shortages, delayed commercialization, and unnecessary emissions.

Yet building reliable models, calibrating them against plant data, and evaluating improvements remains slow, manual, and specialized. Limited engineering capacity leaves valuable improvements unexplored and new processes expensive to scale. We encountered that constraint through our own research and simulation work and started Dualizer to make rigorous process design and optimization accessible throughout a plant’s life.

question_answers.question: What is your long-term vision? If you truly succeed, what will be different about the world?
question_answers.answer:
Our ambition is to make Dualizer the engineering foundation for the world’s process industries—enabling startups and global manufacturers alike to accelerate process development, scale production, and maximize plant performance.

If we succeed, industry will produce more from existing assets, commercialize breakthroughs faster, and make essential goods cheaper and more abundant—with less capital, energy, and material required per unit of output.

In practice, that could mean:

* **Greater energy security:** Increasing throughput and reducing costs across gas processing, LNG, refining, and fuel production.
* **More productive industrial capital:** Unlocking capacity in chemical, fertilizer, cement, and materials plants while reducing the need for costly expansions.
* **Faster AI and electrification growth:** Scaling mineral refining, battery materials, and the high-purity chemicals and gases needed for semiconductor manufacturing.
* **Profitable industrial decarbonization:** Making lower-carbon fuels, hydrogen, cement, and carbon capture competitive at commercial scale.
